rounds.text: Onix Solar Energy Ltd exhibits exceptional top-line and bottom-line velocity, with compounded sales growth reaching 463% and compounded profit growth surging to 2071% over the trailing twelve months [E14, E15]. This stellar fundamental momentum vastly outpaces the broader sector benchmarks, where sector median sales growth sits at 25.0% and profit growth at 46.0% [E58, E59]. The company's market position is strongly reinforced by core insiders, as promoters have aggressively increased their holding by 33.26 percentage points from 19.89% in Dec 2023 to 53.15% as of Sep 2026, alongside an additional recent quarterly increase [E31, E47]. Balance-sheet strength underpins this expansion, with the business remaining conservatively financed at a debt-to-equity ratio of just 0.07x and boasting a comfortable short-term liquidity current ratio of 7.44x [E27, E28]. Furthermore, the valuation is anchored by a modest price-to-book ratio of 1.47x against a book value of ₹ 214, trading favourably compared to the sector benchmark price-to-book of 1.82x [E2, E7]. Conceded: operating cash flow turned negative to Rs -236 Cr in Mar 2026, leading to a weak cash conversion of -7.61x and high working capital days [E24, E25, E51].

Onix Solar Energy Ltd presents a significant disconnect between its market valuation and its underlying operational reality. While the company reports accounting profits, it suffers from a severe cash flow crisis, evidenced by a negative operating and free cash flow of Rs 236 Cr in March 2026 [E25, E26]. This is further underscored by a disastrous cash conversion ratio of -7.61x, suggesting that reported earnings are not translating into actual liquidity [E24]. The company’s efficiency metrics are also concerning, with ROE and ROCE trailing sector benchmarks [E9, E10], and working capital days ballooning from 148 to 494 days [E51]. Furthermore, the stock is priced for perfection, trading at a P/E of 36.08x against a sector benchmark of 14.36x [E6], while a discounted cash flow analysis suggests the current price is overvalued by 64.4% [E35]. Conceded: the company maintains a conservative debt-to-equity ratio of 0.07x [E27] and has seen significant promoter buying [E31]. However, this is overshadowed by the fact that promoters have pledged 94.5% of their holdings [E49], creating substantial risk for shareholders.

Conceded: operating cash flow and free cash flow were negative at Rs -236 Cr in March 2026 [E25, E26], alongside a cash conversion of -7.61x [E24]. However, the bear's claim of a severe financial crisis ignores the company's bulletproof balance sheet boasting a current ratio of 7.44x [E28] and an almost debt-free status with a debt-to-equity ratio of just 0.07x [E27, E46]. While efficiency ratios like ROE and ROCE are highlighted, the company has delivered staggering fundamental momentum through a compounded sales growth of 463% [E14] and a compounded profit growth of 2071% [E15], massively outstripping the sector median sales growth of 25.0% and profit growth of 46.0% [E58, E59]. On valuation multiples, the bear focuses on the P/E of 36.08x [E6], but ignores the price-to-book ratio of 1.36x which actually sits below the sector benchmark of 1.82x [E7]. Furthermore, insider conviction tells the true growth story: promoters have massively increased their stake by 33.26 percentage points from Dec 2023 to Sep 2026 [E31], demonstrating supreme confidence that far outweighs static backward-looking models.

Conceded: promoter holding increased by 33.26 percentage points from Dec 2023 to Sep 2026 [E31], and the price-to-book ratio is 1.36x against a sector benchmark of 1.82x [E7]. However, citing a bulletproof balance sheet with a current ratio of 7.44x [E28] and debt-to-equity of 0.07x [E27] ignores the catastrophic reality that borrowings spiked from Rs 0 Cr to Rs 57 Cr in March 2026 [E29] while operating and free cash flows cratered to a negative Rs -236 Cr [E25, E26]. Conceded: compounded sales growth reached 463% [E14] and profit growth hit 2071% [E15], but this backward-looking momentum is entirely undermined by recent quarterly screen metrics showing a devastating net profit collapse of -79% YoY and sales plunging -69% YoY [E53, E54]. Furthermore, the bull's dismissal of valuation ignores the fundamental DCF overvaluation of -64.4% [E35] and a reverse DCF implying an aggressive 16.8% earnings growth against a 10.0% base case [E36], all while an alarming 94.5% of promoter holdings are pledged [E49]. Finally, praising insider confidence while overlooking high debtors of 262 days [E50] and ballooning working capital days from 148 to 494 days [E51] masks severe operational deterioration that justifies the overall 39/100 sell rating [E52].
